status: materialized before the freeze; X0004 binds the hash of this file
question: Between 8k (quality reference) and 2k (cheaper, but with a measurable ~5% relative tax), is 4k the operating point that is roughly 2x cheaper than 8k with no meaningful loss?
context: S9 established the tradeoff: 2k is 3.99x cheaper on the same positions and trains slightly worse (d = +0.0008..+0.0012, mean +0.00098, not non-inferior at delta=0.001). The 4k labels for these positions already exist, so the sweet-spot question costs no new teacher compute.

positions.source: the same frozen 9,495 ids as S9/S8 (identical order)

training.regime: fixed updates: MAX_UPDATES 760, BATCH 256 = 194,560 sample presentations for every arm

primary_analysis.quantity: d = test_loss(4k) - test_loss(8k), paired by seed, per width; positive = 4k worse

margin.why: identical to S9 so the three depths sit on one scale

primary_analysis.bounds: separate one-sided 95% lower and upper bounds (t=1.729, df=19)

decision.4K_NONINFERIOR: upper bound < +0.001 at all four widths

primary_analysis.secondary_equivalence: two-sided 95% CI inside [-0.001, +0.001] at every width

secondary_analysis.economics: realized teacher nodes over the same 9,495 positions for 8k, 4k and 2k, so the curve is a cost/quality tradeoff rather than a single comparison

stop_conditions: the 4k observations do not exist for all 9,495 positions
